drug_class: BCR-ABL1 inhibitor (STAMP inhibitor — Specifically Targeting the ABL Myristoyl Pocket)
purpose: Asciminib is used to treat a type of blood cancer called chronic myeloid leukemia (CML). It is used in adults whose leukemia has come back or stopped responding to other treatments, or in adults who have a specific genetic mutation called T315I. It helps keep the cancer under control and slow its progression.
how_it_works: Your leukemia is driven by an abnormal protein called BCR-ABL1 that tells cancer cells to grow out of control. Asciminib works like a lock and key — it attaches to a special spot on that abnormal protein and shuts it off, so the cancer cells can no longer get the signal to grow. Because it targets a different spot than older leukemia medicines, it can work even when those older medicines have stopped being effective.
common_side_effects: Muscle and joint pain, tiredness, nausea, rash, stomach pain, headache, diarrhea, constipation, low blood cell counts (which can increase your risk of infection or bleeding), and high blood pressure.
warnings: Asciminib can cause serious heart problems including irregular heartbeat (QT prolongation) and reduced heart function. It may also cause narrowing of blood vessels in the heart or legs (cardiovascular events) and serious low blood counts. Tell your doctor right away if you have chest pain, shortness of breath, leg pain or swelling, or signs of infection like fever. It can harm an unborn baby, so reliable birth control is important during treatment and for a period after stopping. Always tell your doctor and pharmacist about all other medicines you take, as many medications can interact with asciminib.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 40 mg taken by mouth twice a day (about 12 hours apart) for most patients. If you have the T315I mutation, the dose is higher — 200 mg twice a day. Tablets should be taken on an empty stomach, at least 2 hours before or 1 hour after eating. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush or cut it. Try to take it at the same times each day.
